issue.title: Cannot handle commands sent too fast
issue.body:
Hello,

Here is a bit of a context : The price of the energy (kWh) in my country depends on the day, and also on the time of the day. You can retrieve the price of the next day about 24 hours ago through an api call (and via other means). Some days are expensive, some others are cheap. It usually is always cheap during the night, and it sometimes can be very expensive between 6am and 10pm.
So I use your code to control the temperature level (therefore my budget) of my ASHP.

I have one automation in HA that has two triggers. Both triggers are triggered at the exact same time. First trigger will set the temperature at 19, second trigger (I guess a millisecond later) will update it at 20. Which is fine and according to my logic.
I ran into the following issue : My ASHP ignored the second command (setting it at 20) and only shows 19. I believe it is because my commands are sent back to back, too close to each others, that it could not process the last one ?
Is there a way to solve this through the firmware ?

Currently I believe I solved it introducing a 3 seconds delay in my HA automation + setting the automation to "mode: queued". I need to test it more. Not sure if this is efficient yet.

However, I just flashed the firmware to v6.0.0 : https://github.com/F1p/Mitsubishi-CN105-Protocol-Decode/releases/tag/v6.0.0
Where I can read 
"Supports command queue buffer so HA automations can trigger multiple actions at the same time and these can be written to the FTC when it is available"
Does this quote actually address the problem I am reporting here ?

I have one automation in HA that has two triggers. Both triggers are triggered at the exact same time. First trigger will set the temperature at 19, second trigger (I guess a millisecond later) will update it at 20. Which is fine and according to my logic.
I ran into the following issue : My ASHP ignored the second command (setting it at 20) and only shows 19. I believe it is because my commands are sent back to back, too close to each others, that it could not process the last one ?
Is there a way to solve this through the firmware ?

Currently I believe I solved it introducing a 3 seconds delay in my HA automation + setting the automation to "mode: queued". I need to test it more. Not sure if this is efficient yet.

However, I just flashed the firmware to v6.0.0 : https://github.com/F1p/Mitsubishi-CN105-Protocol-Decode/releases/tag/v6.0.0
Where I can read 
"Supports command queue buffer so HA automations can trigger multiple actions at the same time and these can be written to the FTC when it is available"
Does this quote actually address the problem I am reporting here ?

comment.body:
Yes, this quote fixed in 6.0.0 is exactly your report - previous to this you required 3s delay to allow time for the FTC to process.

Now, in 6.0.0 the bridge will buffer & space the writes to allow the FTC time to process each.

issue.body:
I am seeing a number of crashes coming from GLocationService in my third-party app. The crashes look like the below log. So far all reports have been when the app was in the background, and the devices register in Crashlytics as "Android 15". It seems to be specific to GrapheneOS however, as it does not occur on devices which aren't running GrapheneOS. I have been unable to find which build the users have.
